To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a chemokine receptor antagonist can enhance opioid receptor function via hetero-oligomeric receptor interactions.
the CXCR receptor antagonists enhance the function of the DOP receptor agonist only in the presence the CXCR receptor.
a small-molecule antagonist of the CXCR1/2 chemokine receptors can enhance opioid agonist activity at opioid receptors that are hetero-oligomers with the CXCR1 and CXCR2 chemokines receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel small molecule therapeutic agents that target G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCR) and other proteins.
the development of new drugs that are designed to target specific cell surface receptors.

understanding the molecular mechanisms by which the function of one GPCR can be regulated by the expression of a second GPCR, with a particular focus on the role of receptor oligomerization in these processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CXCR1 and CXCR2 antagonists, SB225002 and SB332244, respectively, are allosteric modulators of the DOP receptor.
the allosteric regulation by the CXCR2 chemokines of the DOP opioid receptor is an important mechanism for the regulation of opioid function in cells in which both receptors are expressed.
a CXCR-2 receptor antagonist can increase the efficacy of DOP receptor opioid agonists by acting as an ‘allosteric regulator’ on a heteromer that includes a CXCR2 and DOP receptor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CXCR1/2 antagonist, reparixin, enhances DOP receptor function by acting as an indirect allosteric regulator, via heterodimerization, of the DOP receptor.
CXCR2 antagonist can enhance the DOP receptor function via alloseteric modulation of CXCR2– DOP receptor heterodimers.

a CXCR 2 receptor antagonist can act as an allosterically enhancing agent at a receptor (the DOP opioid receptor) that has no inherent affinity for it, but only when the CXCR2 and DOP receptors are heterodimers.
The main takeaway from our work is that

allosteric regulation can be used to modulate the function of receptors that have no inherent direct affinity for a small molecule, and this can have important implications for the therapeutic use of small-molecules that are allosteric regulators of receptors.
allosteric modulators of heterodimer partners can enhance the function at the target receptor, and that this effect is not restricted to agonists.
the CXCR1/2 chemokine receptors can be targeted by small-molecule drugs to modulate opioid receptor signaling.
